findings.reason: §9 is the live section whose last build failed precisely because its guard proved nothing, and this leaves the node to invent the predicate that decides both the guard and its positive control, so the delivered guard is undetermined by the plan.
findings.text: §9's revised done-when names the environment the session fixture sets (XDG_CACHE_HOME at the session directory, UV_CACHE_DIR pinned aside, no per-kind override, RECKON_HOME untouched) but never states what the guard *fails on*, and the only statement of that predicate is in the superseded paragraph ("fails the session naming any fixture or test that resolved a root outside the session temporary directory"); applied here, that predicate fires on essentially every test rather than on a leak: `tests/conftest.py:1160-1173` installs `isolated_reckon_home` `autouse=True` and sets `RECKON_HOME` to a per-test temporary directory, and `reckon/_store.py:190-196` resolves `pick-input` and `run-time-profile` through `RECKON_HOME` *before* `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, so `cache_root("pick-input")` — the ledger-index root — resolves outside the session directory for any test that reads a ledger, and the revised bullet 2 ("A test that steers a root through `RECKON_HOME` still steers it") confirms those resolutions are legitimate; the top-line claim "keeps every `_store.cache_root` resolution in the session temporary directory" and its own detail therefore cannot both hold, and a node implementing a guard on the stated predicate reddens the suite it exists to protect, while a guard that merely records leaves the leak it is written for unproven.
